title: Israel National Cyber Directorate warns of phishing messages impersonating the police and the Tax Authority
date_note: The Jerusalem Post page (25 Nov) gives only its own publication day for the directorate's warning; no earlier day is stated.
summary: The Jerusalem Post reports that the Israel National Cyber Directorate received numerous reports over several days of phishing messages posing as government agencies, calling the scale alarming. SMS messages posing as the Israel Police demand payment of a traffic fine; WhatsApp messages posing as the Israel Tax Authority promise a refund and direct users to a malicious Android app. The directorate says the links are designed to steal card details and personal information.
plain: Israel's cyber directorate says it has received numerous reports of fake texts from the police and tax authority that try to steal card details and personal information.
exec: The directorate, as reported by the Jerusalem Post, calls the scale of the phishing distribution alarming; the messages impersonate government agencies.
action: The Israel National Cyber Directorate advises not clicking links in such messages, checking payment demands on the official website, sharing no card details or authentication codes, and installing apps only from official stores.

validation.note: Single publisher (Jerusalem Post) relaying the directorate's warning; the directorate's own page was not read.
